'''Katy Padilla Stout''' (born 1985/1986)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sanantonioreport.org/profile/katy-padilla-stout-2026-candidate-for-texas-23rd-congressional-district/ |title=Katy Padilla Stout &#124; 2026 candidate for Texas' 23rd Congressional District |work=San Antonio Report |date=January 8, 2026 |first=Andrea |last=Drusch}}</ref> is an American attorney and politician who is the member-elect for [[Texas's 23rd congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas|2026 election]].<ref name="TPR"/> She is a member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]].

== Early life and education ==
Padilla Stout was born and raised in [[San Antonio, Texas]].<ref name="SAR">{{cite web |title=Katy Padilla Stout profile |url=https://sanantonioreport.org/profile/katy-padilla-stout-2026-candidate-for-texas-23rd-congressional-district/ |website=San Antonio Report |access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> She attended [[North East Independent School District]] schools and graduated from [[Legacy of Educational Excellence High School|Lee High School]] in 2003.<ref name="SAR" /> She earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in education from the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name="SAR" /> She later obtained a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[South Texas College of Law]].<ref name="SAR" />

== Career ==
Padilla Stout began her career as an elementary school teacher in [[Northside Independent School District]].<ref name="SAR" /> As a teacher, she worked in English as a Second Language (ESL), special education, and gifted and talented programs.<ref name="SAR" /> Her experience working with refugee students influenced her decision to pursue a legal career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Katy Padilla Stout sees opening in Texas 23rd Congressional District |url=https://sanantonioreport.org/katy-padilla-stout-texas-23rd-congressional-district-democrat-nominee/ |website=San Antonio Report |access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref>
After earning her law degree, she became an attorney representing children in the foster care system.<ref name="SAR" /> She has served on the Bexar County Child Welfare Board.<ref name="SAR" />

== Political career ==
Padilla Stout ran for the United States House of Representatives in Texas's 23rd congressional district in 2026 as a Democrat.<ref name="TPR">{{cite web |title=Katy Padilla Stout on The Source |url=https://www.tpr.org/podcast/the-source/2026-03-16/katy-padilla-stout-on-the-source |website=Texas Public Radio |access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> She won a multi-candidate Democratic primary to become her party's nominee.<ref name="TPR" /> Her campaign has emphasized issues affecting working families, rural communities, and border regions.<ref name="TPR" /> She defeated Republican nominee [[Brandon Herrera]] in the general election.<ref>https://www.texastribune.org/2026/11/04/texas-brandon-herrera-katy-padilla-stout-congress-district-23-elections-2026/</ref>

== Personal life ==
Padilla Stout lives in the [[Greater San Antonio]] area.<ref name="SAR" /> She is married and has four children.<ref name="SAR" />
